text: Coryza is a bacterial disease found only in chickens, spreading bird-to-bird and able to affect a whole flock within 10 days. Symptoms: swollen infra-orbital sinuses, nasal discharge, sneezing, and matted eyes; egg production can drop up to 40%; generally no severe respiratory signs and no nervous symptoms; the disease runs a long course, 2–3 weeks. Treatment: Tetracyclines and Erythromycin are effective, given for at least 2 weeks.
